1	---
2	title: "Graphic size and timing"
3	description: Set the size a graphic draws at, fit it to the canvas, and control how its own animation runs when the clip gets longer, shorter or split.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A graphic is drawn fresh at a size you choose, and it has an animation timeline of its own. The **Size** and **Timeline** sections of the **Graphic** sub-tab set both, so you can make a graphic sharp at any size and decide whether its outro follows the end of the clip.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Size', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Timeline']}
12	  tools={['set_graphic', 'set_video', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'roll']}
13	/>
14	
15	## Width and Height
16	
17	**Width** and **Height** are the size the graphic draws at, in whole pixels from 1 to 8192 a side. The graphic's code lays itself out at that size, so text and shapes stay sharp.
18	
19	The **Size** section starts collapsed, and its header shows the size, for example `1920 × 1080`. With several graphic clips selected, a change applies to all of them, and a row shows mixed when they differ.
20	
21	A new graphic takes the size its module asks for, or the canvas's size if it doesn't ask.
22	
23	The graphic is drawn at this size and then placed on the canvas like any other layer. Scaling the clip in the [Picture](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab scales that finished picture. To make a graphic bigger and keep it crisp, raise **Width** and **Height** rather than the scale.
24	
25	Changing the [canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) never changes a graphic's size. [Make Vertical Version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/) is the one exception.
26	
27	## Fit to Canvas
28	
29	**Fit to Canvas** in the **Size** section sets the size to the canvas's, then centres the clip at scale 1. It works on every selected graphic clip, as one undo step called Fit Graphic to Canvas.
30	
31	A graphic can't be larger than 8192 pixels a side, so on a bigger canvas Frame Job tells you why and leaves the clip as it was.
32	
33	## The graphic's own timeline
34	
35	A graphic counts its own frames from its first frame, separately from the project's timeline. The **Timeline** section shows where the clip sits on that count. It appears only when one clip is selected, it starts collapsed, and its header shows the length.
36	
37	| Row | What it shows | What you can do |
38	| --- | --- | --- |
39	| **In** | The graphic frame the clip's first frame shows. | Nothing directly. Trimming the front, rolling the cut before the clip and splitting all move it. |
40	| **Length** | How long the graphic's own timeline runs. | Type a timecode to pin it. |
41	| **Follow Clip** | Whether the graphic's timeline ends when the clip ends. | Tick or untick it. |
42	
43	### Follow Clip
44	
45	**Follow Clip** is on for a new clip. The graphic's timeline ends with the clip, so when you lengthen the clip its outro moves to the new end. Most graphics want this.
46	
47	Unticking **Follow Clip** pins **Length** at its current value. Ticking it again hands the length back to the clip.
48	
49	### Length
50	
51	Typing in **Length** pins it, which unticks **Follow Clip**, and is one undo step called Graphic Length. A pinned graphic keeps its pace however long the clip gets, so the animation doesn't stretch and its outro stays at the same point.
52	
53	The value snaps to a frame and can't be less than one frame. Typing the value the field already shows changes nothing, so untick **Follow Clip** to pin the length as it stands.
54	
55	### Length shorter or longer than the clip
56	
57	When **Length** is pinned shorter than the clip, the graphic keeps counting frames past it, but its progress stays at the end. What you see depends on how the graphic is written:
58	
59	- An animation driven by progress holds its end state.
60	- An animation driven by frame numbers keeps going.
61	
62	When **Length** is pinned longer than the clip, the clip ends before the graphic's timeline does, so a late outro never plays.
63	
64	## Trim a graphic like footage
65	
66	Trimming a graphic clip cuts into its animation, as trimming a video cuts into its footage. [Trim](/editing/trimming/) and [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) work as they do on any clip.
67	
68	| Edit | What happens |
69	| --- | --- |
70	| Trim the start, or roll the cut before the clip | **In** moves, so the animation starts further in. **Length** stays the same, so the outro keeps its timing. |
71	| Trim the end, **Follow Clip** on | The graphic's timeline ends at the clip's new end. |
72	| Trim the end, **Length** pinned | **Length** doesn't change. Shortening the clip can cut off the outro. |
73	| Drag the start earlier | A graphic has no source to run out of, so the start can go back as far as the track allows. **In** moves back and stops at 0. |
74	| [Split](/editing/splitting/) the clip | The second half's **In** moves, so it carries on where the first half left off. Both halves pin **Length** to the original's, which unticks **Follow Clip** on both and keeps the outro at the same point. |
75	| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | The clip stretches or squeezes like a title. A pinned **Length** stays as it was. |
76	
77	## Good to know
78	
79	- Actions can't animate size or timing. With an action selected, the **Size** and **Timeline** sections show ⊘ and always change the clip. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
80	- Adding a [transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) that gives a graphic clip extra frames at its head moves **In** back by the same amount, so the picture stays in step. Where **In** is shorter than the extension it stops at 0, and the graphic's first frame lands on the clip's new first frame.
81	- Changing the [project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) moves a graphic's own timeline onto the new frames. **In** and a pinned **Length** snap to the nearest frame. A graphic that counts in seconds keeps its pace, and one that counts frames runs faster at a higher rate.
82	
83	## Related
84	
85	- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)
86	- [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/)
87	- [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/)
88	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
89

1	---
2	title: "Graphics in a vertical version"
3	description: How Make Vertical Version re-sizes and re-lays your graphics for a tall or square canvas, which older template copies it updates, and which modules it names for you to check.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	[Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) has to turn a wide layout into a tall or square one, and graphics can lay themselves out again where footage can't. This page says what happens to each graphic, and which ones you might want to look at afterwards.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
12	  tools="make_vertical_version"
13	/>
14	
15	## Canvas-sized graphics
16	
17	A graphic exactly the old canvas's size, each side, is re-sized to the new canvas, so the module lays itself out again on the new frame. This is usually a full-frame lower third or title card. A 1920 × 1080 graphic on a 1920 × 1080 canvas becomes 1080 × 1920 for 9:16.
18	
19	Its position shrinks and stretches with the two sides of the canvas, and so do the positions its [actions](/graphics/animate-properties/) move it to. Its scale stays as it was, because the graphic is the canvas's size again.
20	
21	This is the one change of canvas that changes a graphic's size. Everywhere else, [Width and Height](/graphics/size-and-timing/#width-and-height) stay as you set them.
22	
23	## Graphics of any other size
24	
25	Any other graphic is kept as placed and rescaled from the old canvas, like a title. That includes a graphic with the same area as the canvas but another shape, such as 1080 × 1920 on a 1920 × 1080 canvas.
26	
27	## Templates measured by the short side
28	
29	These [bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) measure themselves by the canvas's short side, so they fit a tall frame:
30	
31	- Lower third
32	- Title card
33	- Callout
34	- Bar chart
35	- Counter
36	- Kinetic type
37	
38	They draw exactly as before on a landscape or square canvas.
39	
40	## Older template copies
41	
42	A project can hold an older copy of one of those six, inserted before they measured by the short side. Frame Job looks at every module a clip draws, on the timeline and inside nests, and recognises these by their text, never their name. A copy you renamed `intro` is still found.
43	
44	What happens next depends on **Make a copy** in the sheet:
45	
46	| **Make a copy** | What happens |
47	| --- | --- |
48	| Ticked | The copy that opens has each older module rewritten with the current template. Your earlier text is kept as the module's previous version, so [File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…](/graphics/manage-graphics/) brings it back. The project you started from never changes. |
49	| Unticked | Nothing is rewritten, and the summary names each module. |
50	
51	## Your own modules
52	
53	A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height, with `ctx.height / 1080` in its text, is named in the summary, because it may not fit the narrow frame. This applies with or without **Make a copy**, and the module is never rewritten.
54	
55	A template you've edited counts as your own, since its text no longer matches any template Frame Job shipped.
56	
57	To fix one of these, measure by the short side instead:
58	
59	```js
60	const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
61	```
62	
63	On a landscape canvas that's the same number as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a tall canvas drawing the graphic 1.78 times too big. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
64	
65	## What the summary says
66	
67	The sheet's summary reports all of this before you choose **Make**, and it stays accurate as you change the sheet.
68	
69	| The summary says | What it means |
70	| --- | --- |
71	| "Re-sizes 2 graphics to the new canvas." | That many canvas-sized graphics are being re-sized. |
72	| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | That many older template copies are rewritten in the copy. |
73	| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it is an older copy of the bundled template "lower-third"; Make Vertical updates it only in a copy." | You've unticked **Make a copy**. Tick it to update the module. |
74	| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it sizes itself by the canvas's height, so it may not fit the narrow frame." | Check this graphic on the new canvas. |
75	
76	## Related
77	
78	- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
79	- [What a vertical version changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
80	- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)
81	- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)
82

1	---
2	title: "Animate graphic properties"
3	description: Use an action to move a graphic's numbers and colours over time, switch its text and pictures at a set moment, and keep some properties out of the animation.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	A graphic's [properties](/graphics/properties/) can change over time, in the same way an [action](/motion/actions/) moves a clip's position or fades its opacity. Use this to slide a bar's size, change an accent colour, or swap a line of text part way through a clip.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
14	  keys="⌥⌘K"
15	  where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties, with an action selected"
16	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_graphic']}
17	/>
18	
19	## Animate with an action
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Select the graphic clip, move the playhead to where the change should start, and choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>).
24	
25	2. With the action selected, open the **Graphic** sub-tab.
26	
27	3. In **Properties**, set the values the graphic should end at. Each row you change gets a ◆.
28	
29	4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the change.
30	
31	</Steps>
32	
33	<Shot
34	  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.inspector"
35	  alt="The Clip tab with action 1 selected on a graphic clip. The Graphic sub-tab and the Properties section each show a count of 3. The accent, size and boxed rows have a diamond in their gutter, and boxed says at end. The Size and Timeline sections show the ⊘ mark."
36	/>
37	
38	While an action is selected, the **Properties** rows edit the action's end, not the clip. A value you set is kept as you set it, even when it equals the module's default. **Size** and **Timeline** always edit the clip, and they show ⊘.
39	
40	The graphic gets the current values on every frame, and any animation the module does for itself still runs on top.
41	
42	To stop animating a property, take it out of the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action).
43	
44	## What ramps
45	
46	Numbers and colours move along the action's curve from start to end.
47	
48	**A number** arrives with decimals. Going from 64 to 129, it's 96.5 halfway, and it's never rounded or snapped to the property's step.
49	
50	**A colour** blends through OKLab, which keeps the middle of the blend clean, and its transparency blends as a separate value. `#ff0000` to `#0000ff` is `#8c53a2` halfway, and `#ffffff` to `#00000000` is `#63636380`, a half-transparent grey.
51	
52	While a property moves, every frame has to be drawn anew. A graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the length of the action. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).
53	
54	:::caution
55	A module that needs whole numbers has to round them itself, or mark the property [`animate: false`](#stop-a-property-animating). One that does neither can fail on a fraction. Those frames draw the error card, and an export stops there.
56	:::
57	
58	## What switches
59	
60	Text, checkboxes, pop-ups and pictures can't blend. They hold their value through the action, then change to the end's value as the action ends. Their rows say "at end".
61	
62	For a picture, choosing **None** in the pop-up means no picture from the end of the action.
63	
64	## Where an animated property starts
65	
66	An action starts from the value in force when it begins. That's the clip's own value, or what an earlier action finished on.
67	
68	If the clip holds no value for a property, the first action to name it starts from the module's default at that moment. That default is written into the clip in the same undo step, so changing the default later doesn't move the animation.
69	
70	Resetting the clip's own value for a property an action animates sets it to the default, so the action still has somewhere to start from.
71	
72	## Stop a property animating
73	
74	A module can mark any property with `animate: false`, and no action will ever animate it. Modules use this for a count, a layout mode or a data series, where a value part way between two others would break the drawing.
75	
76	The property's row shows ⊘, and it edits the clip even while an action is selected.
77	
78	If you write modules, it's one more key on the schema entry. It must be `true` or `false`, and anything else stops the module compiling. Leaving it out means `true`.
79	
80	```js
81	export const schema = {
82	  count: { type: "number", default: 5, min: 1, max: 20, step: 1, animate: false },
83	};
84	```
85	
86	See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) or **Help ▸ Graphics Reference**.
87	
88	## Values and the module
89	
90	Each value in an action is checked against the module as it is now, including any minimum and maximum. That has a few effects when the module changes after you've animated it:
91	
92	- A value already stored isn't checked again, so narrowing a range later leaves the old end value in place.
93	- If an action names a property the module no longer declares, or no longer lets animate, the row shows dimmed with **⌫**. Choose it to take the property out of the action.
94	- While the module is missing or won't compile, the **Properties** section has no rows to edit, and reads "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below." You can still take values out of the action with **⌫**.
95	
96	## The badge
97	
98	The **Graphic** sub-tab shows a **◆N** badge counting how many properties the selected action animates. The **Properties** section header shows the same count. See [Read the sections and sub-tabs](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-sections-and-sub-tabs).
99	
100	On the timeline, an action's band names a graphic's animated properties along with anything else the action changes, when the track is tall enough to show the label.
101	
102	## With an agent
103	
104	An agent works the same way, adding an action and then naming the end values with `set_action_end`. It can't set a value on a property marked `animate: false` that way, and sets it on the clip with `set_graphic` instead. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
105	
106	## Related
107	
108	- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
109	- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
110	- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
111	- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
112	- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)

1	---
2	title: "Paste Graphic Properties"
3	description: Copy the text, colours and other properties of one graphic clip onto other clips drawn by the same graphic, and see what stays behind.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Paste Graphic Properties copies what one graphic clip shows, its text and colours included, onto other clips drawn by the same graphic. Use it to give a run of lower thirds the same styling, then change the names.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties"
13	  tools="paste_attributes"
14	/>
15	
16	## Paste graphic properties
17	
18	<Steps>
19	
20	1. Select the graphic clip you want to copy from and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
21	
22	2. Select the clips to paste onto.
23	
24	3. Choose **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
25	
26	</Steps>
27	
28	Every selected clip drawn by the same graphic takes the copied properties, as one undo step. The menu item is on when there are Frame Job clips on the clipboard and at least one graphic clip is selected.
29	
30	## What moves and what stays
31	
32	The target ends up with exactly the copied clip's properties, so a property left at its default on the copied clip goes back to the default on the target.
33	
34	Each target keeps:
35	
36	- Its own module, size, **In** and **Length**.
37	- Its position, scale and everything else outside the **Properties** section.
38	- Any property the copied clip leaves unset and an action on the target animates, so that the action keeps its start.
39	
40	If you copied several clips, only the earliest one is read.
41	
42	## When it does nothing
43	
44	| What you'll see | Why |
45	| --- | --- |
46	| Some selected clips don't change | They're drawn by another graphic, or they aren't graphics. They're skipped. |
47	| A beep | The copied clip isn't a graphic, no selected clip is drawn by the same graphic, or the targets already match. |
48	| An alert | The copied properties can't be stored, for example more than 64 of them. It gives the reason, and nothing changes. |
49	
50	## How it differs from Paste Attributes
51	
52	**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) copies a clip's look, such as its position and opacity, and never carries graphic properties. The two are separate on purpose, because a graphic's properties hold its words as well as its look.
53	
54	| | Paste Attributes | Paste Graphic Properties |
55	| --- | --- | --- |
56	| Position, scale, opacity and other picture settings | Yes | No |
57	| A graphic's text, colours and other properties | No | Yes |
58	
59	See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
60	
61	## Copying a graphic clip
62	
63	Copying and pasting a graphic clip (<kbd>⌘C</kbd>, <kbd>⌘V</kbd>) pastes a clip that names its module. The module's `.js` file, fonts and pictures are not copied.
64	
65	So in another project without that module, the pasted clip draws the red error card. To fix it, add the module under the same name, for example with **From File…** in **Insert ▸ Graphic…** on a file of that name. **From File…** also places a clip of its own, which you can delete.
66	
67	See [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).
68	
69	## With an agent
70	
71	An agent uses `paste_attributes` and has to ask for the graphic group by name, since it's never part of the default set. Unlike the menu item, a clip drawn by another graphic stops the paste with an error, unless the agent asks to skip those. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).
72	
73	## Related
74	
75	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
76	- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
77	- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)

1	---
2	title: "Fonts and pictures in graphics"
3	description: Add fonts and pictures to a project's graphics, find the exact font name a graphic must use, and see why a font or picture doesn't draw.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A graphic draws only with the fonts bundled with Frame Job and the fonts and pictures you add to the project, so it looks the same on any Mac. This page covers adding them, and what to do when one doesn't draw.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…', 'File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…']}
13	  tools={['import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'get_graphic']}
14	/>
15	
16	## Add a font
17	
18	<Steps>
19	
20	1. Choose **File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
21	
22	2. Pick a `.ttf` or `.otf` file.
23	
24	</Steps>
25	
26	Frame Job copies the file into the project's `graphics/fonts/` folder, and every graphic in the project can then use it, straight away. Nothing is shown when it works.
27	
28	A file with the same name replaces the old one. If the file holds no font Frame Job can load, an alert says so and nothing is added.
29	
30	## Use the exact family name
31	
32	The family name a graphic must use is the one the graphics engine reads from the file. It can differ from the name Font Book or other apps show.
33	
34	If a font doesn't draw, select the clip and open **Source** in the **Graphic** sub-tab. Under "Checked at the clip's first frame" it reports the missing family and lists every family the project has, so you can copy the exact name from there. The section's header shows "1 warning" when there's something to read.
35	
36	The check looks at the clip's first frame only, so a font used later in the animation isn't reported there.
37	
38	## Bundled fonts
39	
40	These seven families draw on every Mac, with nothing to install.
41	
42	| Family | Weights |
43	| --- | --- |
44	| Anton | 400 |
45	| Bebas Neue | 400 |
46	| Darker Grotesque | Variable, 300 to 900 |
47	| IBM Plex Mono | 400, 500 |
48	| Montserrat | 800, 900 |
49	| Source Sans 3 | Variable, 200 to 900 |
50	| Source Serif 4 | Variable, 200 to 900 |
51	
52	## Generic families
53	
54	A module can also ask for a generic family, which draws in a bundled face.
55	
56	| Generic | Draws in |
57	| --- | --- |
58	| `serif` | Source Serif 4 |
59	| `sans-serif` | Source Sans 3 |
60	| `monospace` | IBM Plex Mono |
61	
62	Write a generic without quotes, as in `font-family="sans-serif"`. With quotes it names a family called "sans-serif", which isn't there. `cursive` and `fantasy` aren't available.
63	
64	## System fonts
65	
66	Graphics never use the fonts installed on your Mac, so a project draws the same everywhere. To use one of them, add its file to the project with [Add Font to Graphics](#add-a-font).
67	
68	What happens to a family name in a module:
69	
70	- A family the project doesn't have draws nothing, with a warning naming the families it does have.
71	- In a list such as `"Nope, Montserrat"`, the first family the project has draws.
72	- A family with a word starting with a digit must be quoted, as in `font-family="'Source Sans 3'"`. Unquoted, it draws nothing, with a warning.
73	
74	:::note
75	[Text clips](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) work differently, and do use the fonts on your Mac.
76	:::
77	
78	## Add a picture
79	
80	<Steps>
81	
82	1. Choose **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
83	
84	2. Pick a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ file.
85	
86	</Steps>
87	
88	Frame Job copies the file into the project's `graphics/assets/` folder. A module can then draw it, and a [picture property's](/graphics/properties/) pop-up lists it.
89	
90	A file with the same name replaces the old one. Any other kind of file can't be added, and an empty file gets an alert and isn't added.
91	
92	## Picture names
93	
94	A module refers to a picture by its file name, and some names can't be used that way. A name is not usable when it:
95	
96	- Starts with `.` or `#`.
97	- Holds any of `/ : " ' < > &`, or a control character.
98	- Is longer than 247 bytes.
99	
100	A picture with a name like that is added under a legal one, and a notice tells you which:
101	
102	> `"#logo&mark.png" was added as "logo-mark.png": asset(name) cannot use the name it had.`
103	
104	If the legal name is taken, the picture takes `-2`, `-3` and so on, as in `logo-mark-2.png`. A renamed copy never replaces an existing file.
105	
106	## Drop files in the folder
107	
108	You can also put fonts and pictures straight into `graphics/fonts/` and `graphics/assets/` with the Finder or any other tool. Frame Job notices within a moment.
109	
110	To find the folder, choose **Reveal in Finder** in the **Source** section of a graphic clip. It shows the module's file inside `graphics/`. If `fonts` or `assets` isn't there yet, make a folder with exactly that name.
111	
112	Anything the folder scan can't use is skipped, with a warning in **Source** under "In the graphics folder":
113	
114	- A font that doesn't load.
115	- An empty picture.
116	- A picture with a name a module can't use. Unlike a picture added from the menu, it isn't renamed for you.
117	
118	## Good to know
119	
120	- Neither import is an undo step. To take a file out, delete it from the folder.
121	- Fonts and pictures belong to the project. Another project needs its own copy.
122	- Both menu items work as soon as the project window is open. There's no need to save first.
123	
124	## With an agent
125	
126	An agent can read the exact family names directly, rather than waiting for a warning. `get_graphic` lists them, and `import_graphic_font` answers with the names a new file adds. See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).
127	
128	## Related
129	
130	- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
131	- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
132	- [The module API](/graphics/module-api/)
133	- [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/)

2	// 10 §5j, G5a): Source (in `GraphicPane+Source.swift`), Properties from the

9	// Timeline still write `set_graphic`, so their rows are ⊘. The core

18	// and `length` are that clip's own. With different modules Source says so

22	// main only), the same read `AgentServer+Graphics.compiledModule` makes for

24	// is not re-entrant (road map 10 §10.6 G3a).

28	extension InspectorBinding {
29	    /// The selected clips drawn by a module.
30	    var graphicClips: [ClipSnapshot] {
31	        clips.filter { clip in
32	            if case .graphic = clip.source { return clip.graphic != nil }
33	            return false
34	        }
35	    }
36	}

38	final class GraphicPane: InspectorPaneView {
39	    /// The report of each module/revision/library/frame hash/size seen, and
40	    /// the last report per clip — what a miss answers while a live gesture
41	    /// runs, so the signature holds still through a drag.
42	    var reportMemo: [String: GraphicClipReport] = [:]
43	    var lastReports: [UInt32: GraphicClipReport] = [:]
44	    /// The parsed schema of the last module asked, keyed "name|revision".
45	    var schemaMemo: (key: String, schema: GraphicSchema)?
46	    /// Each clip's recipe layer source under `layerProject`, the handle it
47	    /// was read from; emptied when the binding's project is another handle.
48	    weak var layerProject: ReelProject?
49	    var layerMemo: [UInt32: RecipeSourceRef] = [:]
50	
51	    /// Whether the graphic sections apply: they write `set_graphic`, which
52	    /// errors on any other kind, so a mixed selection gets none of them.
53	    var allGraphic: Bool {
54	        !binding.clips.isEmpty && binding.graphicClips.count == binding.clips.count
55	    }
56	
57	    /// The one module every selected graphic clip is drawn by.
58	    struct Shared {
59	        let name: String
60	        let file: GraphicModuleFile?
61	        let entry: GraphicRegistry.Entry?
62	    }
63	
64	    /// nil when the selection's modules differ (or it holds no graphic).
65	    func shared() -> Shared? {
66	        let names = Set(binding.graphicClips.compactMap { $0.graphic?.name })
67	        guard names.count == 1, let name = names.first else { return nil }
68	        let document = binding.document
69	        return Shared(
70	            name: name, file: document?.graphicStore?.module(named: name),
71	            entry: document.flatMap {
72	                GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(named: name, for: $0.recipeKey)
73	            })
74	    }
75	
76	    /// The compiled schema of `shared`, parsed in the module's order, and
77	    /// the registry's dictionary the ops carry. Parsed once per name and
78	    /// revision (`schemaMemo`).
79	    func schema(_ shared: Shared?) -> (schema: GraphicSchema, raw: [String: Any])? {
80	        guard let shared, case .compiled(let module, let revision, _, let raw)? = shared.entry
81	        else { return nil }
82	        let key = "\(shared.name)|\(revision)"
83	        if let memo = schemaMemo, memo.key == key { return (memo.schema, raw) }
84	        let parsed = GraphicSchema(describeJSON: module.describeJSON(), schema: raw)
85	        schemaMemo = (key, parsed)
86	        return (parsed, raw)
87	    }
88	
89	    /// The selection's stored props, merged; the first clip holding a key wins.
90	    func storedProps() -> [String: GraphicPropValue] {
91	        var merged: [String: GraphicPropValue] = [:]
92	        for clip in binding.graphicClips {
93	            merged.merge(clip.graphic?.props ?? [:]) { first, _ in first }
94	        }
95	        return merged
96	    }
97	
98	    /// The selected action's end props (G-34 (a)); none with no action
99	    /// selected. Its keys the schema lacks are the action's stale rows.
100	    func endProps() -> [String: GraphicPropValue] {
101	        binding.selectedAction?.end.graphic?.props ?? [:]
102	    }
103	
104	    /// The asset folder's file names, sorted.
105	    func assetNames() -> [String] {
106	        (binding.document?.graphicStore?.scan.assets.map(\.name) ?? []).sorted()
107	    }
108	
109	    /// What the graphics folder's scan skipped or could not watch, in its own
110	    /// sentences — the Source section's folder rows (G-24 (b)).
111	    func folderWarnings() -> [String] {
112	        binding.document?.graphicStore?.scan.warnings ?? []
113	    }
114	
115	    /// The schema's entries whole (a default, bounds or options a row is
116	    /// built from), the stale keys (the clip's, then the selected action's
117	    /// end's, `actionStaleKeys`, a declared key no action may animate
118	    /// included, G-41), each asset popup's names (the selected end's
119	    /// included, G-42), the
120	    /// diagnostics' messages and the folder's warnings. Stored values, the
121	    /// revision and the playhead are NOT here: they are read fresh by
122	    /// `refresh()`.
123	    override var structureSignature: String {
124	        guard allGraphic else { return super.structureSignature + "|-" }
125	        let shared = self.shared()
126	        let parsed = schema(shared)
127	        let keys = parsed?.schema.entries.map { String(describing: $0) } ?? []
128	        let stale = GraphicSchemaRows.staleKeys(stored: storedProps(), schema: parsed?.schema)
129	        var messages = ["-", "-"]
130	        if let shared, let clip = binding.graphicClips.first, let document = binding.document {
131	            let version = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)?.libraryVersion
132	            let report = self.report(for: clip, shared, libraryVersion: version ?? "")
133	            func spell(_ list: [GraphicDiagnostic]) -> String {
134	                list.map { "\($0.level):\($0.line ?? -1):\($0.column ?? -1):\($0.message)" }
135	                    .joined(separator: "¶")
136	            }
137	            messages = [spell(report.compile), spell(report.render)]
138	        }
139	        messages.append(folderWarnings().joined(separator: "¶"))
140	        return [
141	            super.structureSignature, shared?.name ?? "mixed", keys.joined(separator: ","),
142	            stale.joined(separator: ","), assetSignature(parsed?.schema),
143	            GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleKeys(end: endProps(), schema: parsed?.schema)
144	                .joined(separator: ","),
145	        ].joined(separator: "|") + "|" + messages.joined(separator: "|")
146	    }
147	
148	    /// Each asset entry's popup names, from the rows' own
149	    /// `GraphicSchemaRows.assetNames` call, the selected action's end's names
150	    /// counting (G-42 (d)): names joined by ",", entries by ";".
151	    private func assetSignature(_ schema: GraphicSchema?) -> String {
152	        let files = assetNames(), clips = binding.graphicClips
153	        return (schema?.entries ?? []).filter { $0.type == "asset" }.map {
154	            GraphicSchemaRows.assetNames(for: $0, files: files, clips: clips, end: endProps())
155	                .joined(separator: ",")
156	        }.joined(separator: ";")
157	    }
158	
159	    // MARK: - Properties
160	
161	    /// One row per schema key in the module's order, then the stale keys,
162	    /// sorted, then — with an action selected — the end's own stale keys
163	    /// (G-34 (l), O2), a declared key whose entry is not `animatable` among
164	    /// them (G-41 (c)). With no compiled schema every stored key is stale.
165	    /// Reset nulls every stored key; with an action selected it writes each
166	    /// declared default through the rows' own split, into the END (an
167	    /// asset's `null` as `""`, G-42 (d)), an `animate: false` prop's (G-41
168	    /// (d)) onto the clip (O7). Its `differs` folds from the rows.
169	    func propertiesSection() -> InspectorSection {
170	        let binding = self.binding
171	        let shared = self.shared()
172	        let parsed = schema(shared)
173	        let clips = { binding.graphicClips }
174	        let assets = { [weak self] in self?.assetNames() ?? [] }
175	        var rows: [NSView] = parsed?.schema.entries.map {
176	            GraphicSchemaRows.row(
177	                $0, binding, clips: clips, schema: parsed?.raw ?? [:], assets: assets)
178	        } ?? []
179	        let stored = storedProps()
180	        for key in GraphicSchemaRows.staleKeys(stored: stored, schema: parsed?.schema) {
181	            rows.append(
182	                GraphicSchemaRows.staleRow(
183	                    key: key, value: stored[key] ?? .null, binding, clips: clips))
184	        }
185	        let ends = endProps()
186	        let declared = Set(parsed?.schema.keys ?? [])
187	        for key in GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleKeys(end: ends, schema: parsed?.schema) {
188	            rows.append(
189	                GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleRow(
190	                    key: key, value: ends[key] ?? .null, declared: declared.contains(key), binding))
191	        }
192	        let note: String?
193	        if parsed == nil {
194	            note = "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below."
195	        } else if parsed?.schema.entries.isEmpty == true {
196	            note = "The module declares no properties."
197	        } else {
198	            note = nil
199	        }
200	        let count = parsed?.schema.entries.count ?? 0
201	        return InspectorSection(
202	            id: "graphic.properties", title: "Properties",
203	            summary: { count == 1 ? "1 property" : "\(count) properties" },
204	            note: note.map { text -> () -> String? in { text } },
205	            reset: {
206	                if binding.selectedAction != nil {
207	                    let entries = parsed?.schema.entries ?? []
208	                    let defaults = Dictionary(
209	                        entries.map { ($0.key, $0.default) }, uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })
210	                    binding.apply(
211	                        "Reset Graphic Properties",
212	                        binding.ops(
213	                            graphic: defaults, entries: entries, clips: clips(), schema: parsed?.raw))
214	                    return
215	                }
216	                let targets = clips()
217	                var keys = Set<String>()
218	                for clip in targets { keys.formUnion(clip.graphic?.props.keys.map { $0 } ?? []) }
219	                guard !keys.isEmpty else { return NSSound.beep() }
220	                binding.apply(
221	                    "Reset Graphic Properties",
222	                    [GraphicSchemaRows.op(
223	                        clips: targets,
224	                        props: Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: keys.map { ($0, NSNull()) }),
225	                        schema: parsed?.raw)])
226	            },
227	            defaultExpanded: true,
228	            rows: rows)
229	    }
230	
231	    // MARK: - Size
232	
233	    /// Width and height, fanned out one op per clip in one apply, and Fit to
234	    /// Canvas: the canvas's size, centred at scale 1.
235	    func sizeSection() -> InspectorSection {
236	        let binding = self.binding
237	        func first() -> GraphicSnapshot? { binding.graphicClips.first?.graphic }
238	        func side(_ key: String, _ value: Double) -> [ReelOp] {
239	            binding.graphicClips.map {
240	                .setGraphicRaw(clips: [$0.id], patch: [key: Int(value.rounded())])
241	            }
242	        }
243	        return InspectorSection(
244	            id: "graphic.size", title: "Size",
245	            summary: { first().map { "\($0.width) × \($0.height)" } },
246	            defaultExpanded: false,
247	            rows: [
248	                inspectorValueRow(
249	                    "Width", binding, name: "Graphic Size", unit: " px", min: 1,
250	                    max: Double(GraphicLibrary.maxSide), slider: false,
251	                    width: InspectorMetrics.wideFieldWidth,
252	                    read: { Double(first()?.width ?? 0) }, ops: { side("width", $0) },
253	                    mixed: { binding.mixed(binding.graphicClips) { $0.graphic?.width } },
254	                    resets: false),
255	                inspectorValueRow(
256	                    "Height", binding, name: "Graphic Size", unit: " px", min: 1,
257	                    max: Double(GraphicLibrary.maxSide), slider: false,
258	                    width: InspectorMetrics.wideFieldWidth,
259	                    read: { Double(first()?.height ?? 0) }, ops: { side("height", $0) },
260	                    mixed: { binding.mixed(binding.graphicClips) { $0.graphic?.height } },
261	                    resets: false),
262	                inspectorButtonRow([
263	                    inspectorButton(
264	                        "Fit to Canvas", binding, name: "Fit Graphic to Canvas",
265	                        ops: { Self.fitToCanvasOps(clips: binding.graphicClips, canvas: binding.canvas) }),
266	                ]),
267	            ])
268	    }
269	
270	    /// Per clip: the canvas's size, then the layer centred at scale 1.
271	    static func fitToCanvasOps(clips: [ClipSnapshot], canvas: CanvasSnapshot) -> [ReelOp] {
272	        clips.flatMap { clip -> [ReelOp] in
273	            [
274	                .setGraphicRaw(
275	                    clips: [clip.id], patch: ["width": canvas.width, "height": canvas.height]),
276	                .setVideo(clips: [clip.id], patch: VideoPatch(x: 0, y: 0, scale: 1)),
277	            ]
278	        }
279	    }
280	
281	    // MARK: - Timeline
282	
283	    /// The graphic's own timeline (G-9): In, read-only — the point
284	    /// `trim_start`, `roll` and `split` move — and Length, typed, which pins
285	    /// it; Follow Clip gives it back to the clip (`null`, which ends it at
286	    /// `in + duration`, G-9·c).
287	    ///
288	    /// Binds by clip ID and reads fresh through it, `timingSection`'s rule.
289	    func timelineSection(_ id: UInt32) -> InspectorSection {
290	        let binding = self.binding
291	        func clip() -> ClipSnapshot? { binding.snapshot.clip(id) }
292	        func fps() -> Fps { binding.canvas.fps }
293	        func frames() -> Bool { binding.canvas.timecodeFrames }
294	        func length() -> Ticks {
295	            guard let clip = clip() else { return 0 }
296	            return clip.graphicEffectiveLength ?? clip.duration
297	        }
298	        let field = InspectorTimecodeField(
299	            read: length,
300	            write: { value in
301	                binding.apply("Graphic Length", [.setGraphicRaw(clips: [id], patch: ["length": value])])
302	            },
303	            fps: fps, frames: frames,
304	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
305	        field.toolTip = "How long the graphic's own timeline runs — typing pins it"
306	        return InspectorSection(
307	            id: "graphic.timeline", title: "Timeline",
308	            summary: { ReelTime.format(length(), fps: fps(), frames: frames()) },
309	            defaultExpanded: false,
310	            rows: [
311	                inspectorRow("In", [inspectorReadout {
312	                    ReelTime.format(clip()?.graphic?.sourceIn ?? 0, fps: fps(), frames: frames())
313	                }]),
314	                inspectorRow("Length", [field]),
315	                inspectorCheckRow(
316	                    "Follow Clip", binding, name: "Graphic Follow Clip",
317	                    read: { clip()?.graphic.map { $0.length == nil } ?? true },
318	                    ops: { on in
319	                        [.setGraphicRaw(
320	                            clips: [id], patch: ["length": on ? NSNull() : length() as Any])]
321	                    },
322	                    resets: false),
323	            ])
324	    }
325	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio
  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and
  `gates` a gated clip's hide-while-silent gate (format 43, spec §11 CO-93). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;
  `foreground` and the image arm format 41, CO10a, CO-100, CO-101) holds `CutoutSubject`
  (`person`, `foreground`), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground`, `CutoutProps` (`VideoProps.cutout` and
  `VideoPatch.cutout`; its `dictionary` writes all five keys), `CutoutPatch` (the sparse
  write `VideoPatch.cutoutPart` carries — written under `cutout` only when `cutout` is nil,
  never decoded — so a Background, Edge or Feather row writes its own key alone, CO3),
  `RecipeCutoutMaskKind` (`media`, and `image`, drawn since CO10b from the
  picture's one mask, CO-107),
  `RecipeCutoutMask` (`kind` and `media` required; `subject` lenient,
  `person` when absent, CO-101) and `RecipeCutout` (the recipe layer's
  `cutout`, `mask` required; `subjectCopy`, CO-51); `RecipeLayer.videoProps` passes no cutout — the recipe's is a draw
  instruction, not the clip's props. `VideoProps.swift` (`VideoProps`),
  `ClipSnapshot.swift` (`ClipSource` with its nested `CodingKeys`, `ClipSnapshot`,
  `TransitionSnapshot`) and `TrackSnapshot.swift` (`TrackSnapshot`) are pure moves out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T11–T13). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).
  `TextProps.swift` is the text group and `RecipeReveal` (with format version
  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and
  `InspectorBinding.contentOps` / `ops(textContent:)` — the Content write,
  decided PER CLIP: `words: []` beside the content in one `set_text` only for
  base clips whose count changed, and never `words` in an action end (W-2,
  W-6). It lives there, not in `InspectorPane.swift`, for the size rule.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`, +`Reverse`, +`Derived`)
  — NSDocument, `.framejob` package read/write, and the single mutation

`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,

file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

import glob
import os
import struct
import sys

root = sys.argv[1]
for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*.ttf"))):
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    count = struct.unpack(">H", data[4:6])[0]
    tables = {}
    for i in range(count):
        off = 12 + 16 * i
        tag = data[off:off + 4].decode()
        _, offset, length = struct.unpack(">III", data[off + 4:off + 16])
        tables[tag] = (offset, length)
    weight = None
    if "OS/2" in tables:
        o = tables["OS/2"][0]
        weight = struct.unpack(">H", data[o + 4:o + 6])[0]
    family = None
    if "name" in tables:
        o = tables["name"][0]
        fmt, n, strings = struct.unpack(">HHH", data[o:o + 6])
        names = {}
        for i in range(n):
            p, e, l, nid, ln, so = struct.unpack(">HHHHHH", data[o + 6 + 12 * i:o + 18 + 12 * i])
            if p == 3 and nid in (1, 2, 16, 17):
                names[nid] = data[o + strings + so:o + strings + so + ln].decode("utf-16-be")
        family = names
    axes = []
    if "fvar" in tables:
        o = tables["fvar"][0]
        _, _, axes_off, _, axis_count, axis_size = struct.unpack(">HHHHHH", data[o:o + 12])
        for i in range(axis_count):
            a = o + axes_off + axis_size * i
            tag = data[a:a + 4].decode()
            lo, default, hi = [v / 65536 for v in struct.unpack(">iii", data[a + 4:a + 16])]
            axes.append((tag, lo, default, hi))
    print(os.path.basename(path), "OS/2", weight, family, axes)

import glob
import os
import struct
import sys

root = sys.argv[1]
for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*.ttf"))):
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    count = struct.unpack(">H", data[4:6])[0]
    tables = {}
    for i in range(count):
        off = 12 + 16 * i
        tag = data[off:off + 4].decode()
        _, offset, length = struct.unpack(">III", data[off + 4:off + 16])
        tables[tag] = (offset, length)
    weight = None
    if "OS/2" in tables:
        o = tables["OS/2"][0]
        weight = struct.unpack(">H", data[o + 4:o + 6])[0]
    family = None
    if "name" in tables:
        o = tables["name"][0]
        fmt, n, strings = struct.unpack(">HHH", data[o:o + 6])
        names = {}
        for i in range(n):
            p, e, l, nid, ln, so = struct.unpack(">HHHHHH", data[o + 6 + 12 * i:o + 18 + 12 * i])
            if p == 3 and nid in (1, 2, 16, 17):
                names[nid] = data[o + strings + so:o + strings + so + ln].decode("utf-16-be")
        family = names
    axes = []
    if "fvar" in tables:
        o = tables["fvar"][0]
        _, _, axes_off, _, axis_count, axis_size = struct.unpack(">HHHHHH", data[o:o + 12])
        for i in range(axis_count):
            a = o + axes_off + axis_size * i
            tag = data[a:a + 4].decode()
            lo, default, hi = [v / 65536 for v in struct.unpack(">iii", data[a + 4:a + 16])]
            axes.append((tag, lo, default, hi))
    print(os.path.basename(path), "OS/2", weight, family, axes)

== paste_attributes True
Copies the payload's EARLIEST clip's property groups onto each of the clips — Edit ▸ Paste Attributes (⌥⌘V). The payload is the same Copy payload paste takes; only its earliest clip is read (at one start the front-most, then the lower id — never the array's first, which is creation order), and its ids and media rows do not matter. Each group REPLACES the target's whole group — video and audio whole (position and scale included), text but its content, a shape but its kind, width, height, from and to. Left out, `groups` means each of video, audio, text and shape BOTH clips have, silently skipping the rest; a named group the payload clip lacks, or a target lacks, is an error, and so is a value the inspector would refuse. `graphic` travels only when NAMED (Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties): the props, whole, onto clips drawn by the SAME graphic, each keeping its name, size, in and length, and any prop the payload lacks that an action on that clip animates, which stays so the ramp keeps its start; a clip of another graphic is an error naming both. The props are checked for shape only, when a target takes them. Speed, enabled, actions, the transition and the clip's own name and label stay. A video qualifier follows the clip kind: dropped onto a picture clip, an adjustment clip's own kept when the payload clip is not an adjustment clip, copied between two. Refused (no change) when nothing changes.

Copies a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ file into the project's graphics/assets/ (creating the folders if they are absent), where a module draws it with <image href="${asset(name)}">; answers every asset the folder now holds. Reads the project's graphics/ folder. With name: that module's source, revision (the SHA-256 of its bytes), path, whether it compiles (ok, meta, schema, diagnostics), the clips drawn by it and kept, the revisions of its kept earlier texts, newest first (restore_graphic takes one). The folder may also be edited with your own file tools: modules (<name>.js), fonts in fonts/ (.ttf, .otf) and pictures in assets/; the app sees a change within a moment. guide_errors: docs/guide/graphics.md:350 says the six templates (Lower third, Title card, Callout, Bar chart, Counter, Kinetic type) measure themselves by the canvas's short side, as if only those do. The six are only the ones with older height-sized copies.
